high.title: Shinhan Bank Sees Dollar-Won at 1,490-1,530 in June - 'Neither War Nor Peace, Status Quo Prevails'
high.summary: Shinhan Bank forecasts KRW/USD will trade in a narrow 1,490-1,530 range in June, suggesting limited downside despite ongoing US-Iran ceasefire talks. The bank cites fragile negotiation progress and potential market overreaction ahead of new Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's first FOMC meeting as key constraints. While the US and Iran appear close to a "provisional agreement" extending the 60-day ceasefire and beginning nuclear negotiations, differing interpretations over Strait of Hormuz passage rights keep the deal fragile. This cautious outlook suggests sustained KRW weakness against a backdrop of geopolitical uncertainty and Fed policy transition risks, offering limited relief for Korean exporters or foreign investors seeking KRW exposure.

high.title: Busan Bank Sees Dollar-Won at 1,460-1,530 in June - Foreign Capital Flows to Determine Direction
high.summary: Busan Bank projects KRW/USD in the 1,460-1,530 range for June, identifying foreign capital flows as the critical variable for exchange rate direction. The bank notes that whether foreign selling pressure in Korean equities subsides will be crucial for FX stability. Upward pressure on USD/KRW persists from delayed US-Iran ceasefire talks, reduced Fed rate cut expectations amid inflation concerns, global dollar strength, and continued net foreign equity selling. However, downward factors are building including current account improvements. This analysis highlights the direct link between foreign portfolio flows and KRW performance, suggesting any sustained foreign equity buying could drive meaningful KRW appreciation toward the lower end of the forecast range.

high.title: BOK - Economic Security Paradigm Drives Semiconductor Investment Decisions
high.summary: The Bank of Korea reports that economic security considerations now significantly influence Korea's capital investment decisions, particularly in semiconductors, marking a structural shift from pure efficiency-based allocation. Using SVAR analysis, the BOK found security and global factors' contribution to Korea's investment growth expanded 14.3 percentage points to 43.9% since 2020, up from 29.6% during 2001-2019. Trade policy uncertainty and geopolitical risks specifically expanded their influence by 8.7pp and 4.0pp respectively. This fundamental change in investment drivers has major implications for Korean markets - it suggests more volatile, politically-sensitive capital allocation that could impact sectors differently based on their strategic importance rather than pure profitability, potentially affecting equity valuations and industrial competitiveness.

medium.title: NDF at 1,506.30/1,506.70 Won - Down 0.35 Won
medium.summary: Dollar-won one-month NDF declined 0.35 won to 1,506.50 won in NY trading after Trump mentioned making a "final decision" on Iran peace agreement MOU. The NDF's decline suggests offshore markets are pricing in modest KRW strength on potential geopolitical de-escalation.

medium.title: Iran Foreign Minister Says 'Dialogue and Message Exchange with US Continues'
medium.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister confirmed ongoing dialogue with the US but cautioned against speculation until clear results emerge. This measured tone suggests negotiations remain fluid, maintaining uncertainty that could continue to support safe-haven USD demand and pressure risk-sensitive KRW.

medium.title: Trump Says Iran to Abandon Nuclear Development and Purchases - 'Close to Good Deal'
medium.summary: President Trump indicated the US is "very close to a very good deal" with Iran, suggesting potential breakthrough in negotiations. However, he maintains fallback option of restarting military operations, keeping geopolitical risk premium in markets and limiting potential KRW gains from any agreement.

medium.title: [FX-Weekly] Key Question - US-Iran War End...How Long Will Foreign Equity Outflows Last
medium.summary: Seoul FX market expected to react sensitively to US-Iran MOU signing this week. While agreement appears imminent, continued foreign equity selling is blocking KRW downside support. USD/KRW closed at 1,507.90 won, with risk appetite and oil price movements key variables ahead.

medium.title: [Bond Market - Weekly] May Inflation in Focus Amid Government Stability Pledge; Ceasefire Talks Also Key
medium.summary: Korean bond market this week will digest government's market stabilization commitment through June treasury issuance plan while monitoring US-Iran talks. May CPI data due June 2nd is key domestic indicator, alongside global factors including US employment report on June 5th.
